_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
1/7 2:24PM - Patrol was dropping ropes like they were hot, opening up access to over an additional 240 acres of terrain today! With 6 inches of fresh snow and 579 acres of skiable terrain, today was one for the books! For your Thursday, we plan to make turns down 92 trails with 68 set to receive stripes overnight. 9 lifts are scheduled to spin at 9AM with no anticipated delays. It's shaping up to be another great day tomorrow so rest those legs and I’ll see you bright and early!

The park scene is coming to life with a 13-foot Halfpipe open and firing on East Byrnes Side with 6 features ready to ride. Tyrolinne is also open with 7 features to keep the park laps rolling. 

Operations Update: Snowmaking has been extra active over the past few days, concentrating efforts on Stevek, World Cup, Churchill Downs, Lower Middlebrook, Upper Down Easter, Black Bear, Janeway Junction, Upper and Lower West Meadow, Lower Kidderbrook, Daniel Webster, Big Ben, Upper and Lower East Meadow, and Lower Wanderer. Forecasted warmer temperatures and the chance of rain will temporarily put guns on hold beginning mid-week through this coming weekend. Once cold temperatures return, snowmaking will resume with the next round targeting Upper and Lower East Meadow, Bear Down, Upper Kidderbrook, Free Fall, Upper Standard, Rime Line, Supertrail and Big Ben. A brief warm-up is nothing new for our Operations Team, who will continue working around the clock to deliver the best possible conditions. Be sure to stay tuned to the Mountain Report for more snowmaking and operational updates to come.

Safety Tip: Always ski or ride with a friend in the glades. 

Spots have opened up this weekend on January 10 for a once-in-a-lifetime winter dining experience! Our Snowcat Dinners offer a ride in a snowcat to our Mid-Mountain Lodge, where a seasonal welcome beverage and hors d’oeuvres lead into a candlelit, six-course dinner crafted by our culinary team. If you can’t make it Saturday, we have plenty more dates available this winter season; Book now to secure your spot!

Discover the thrill of skiing or snowboarding with Stratton Mountain's Learn to Ski or Ride Program. This step-by-step program is designed to help you master the slopes—and reward you with a 25/26 Stratton Select Pass, to ride out the rest of the season, upon completion.

Looking to progress this season? Stratton’s Camps and Clinics offer targeted skill development, expert coaching, and a strong sense of community for skiers and snowboarders. From women’s programs to freestyle, snowboard, and advanced clinics, each offers a supportive, goal focused environment to help you make the most of the season, with programs offered all throughout the winter. 

Stay and relish the Green Mountains! Stratton Real Estate is here to help with all your real estate needs. Make your sweet escape a reality.

Reliable cars are the name of the game; that is why we trust Oliver Subaru and Ford. Made for all seasons and all families, check out Oliver Ford and Oliver Subaru for year-round reliability.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report: This week has been stellar…but wait there’s more! Summit Express is expected to open midday today. Dust off your powder skis and boards because It’s going to be soft, steep, and deep up there. Summit Express spinning means Dynamite laps are back, so take a cruise and soak in the views. There’s still plenty of soft snow to be found in the trees in Apex Express and Moonbeam Express terrain. We are expecting temperatures in the low to mid-20’s under mostly cloudy skies. Another storm will roll in today with scattered snowfall starting later this afternoon and evening. The forecasts are spread out, calling for 8 to 20 inches of snow, fingers crossed for another heavy hitter. We are as excited as you for freshies but don’t duck ropes into closed terrain. Unseen hazards exist and you will lose your pass for at least 30 days (at all Ikon Pass resorts). Expert skills are required on Sunrise terrain. The easiest way down from Powderhorn II is to take Eagle Ridge to Sunshine Bowl. Beginners should stick to Link and Moonbeam Express.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Good Morning Skiers and Riders! This is ELI with your 5 am snow report for Wednesday, January 7th. Remember the easiest way to get up to date information is on the Ikon Pass app or website.  

Our Mid mountain base is 25 inches, the temperature is 23 degrees, the winds are 5 miles per hour from the south, with clear skies. 

The Summit base is 37 inches, the temperature is 15 degrees, the winds 20 miles per hour from the southwest. 

The base temperature is 9 degrees.  

We will be skiing and riding on 19 lifts, 99 runs, and 1,199 acres on packed powder snow.  

Musicfest at Steamboat continues today with plenty of free music to enjoy. This afternoon, head down to Steamboat Square for incredible live music set against a classic mountain backdrop. The first band start playing at 12pm, head to steamboat.com/events for the full lineup  

Stay in the know with the Ikon Pass App. Find it in the app store on your mobile device and get lift and trail statuses, conditions updates, and more.  

If you are thinking of exploring outside the ski area boundaries, and don’t know exactly where you are going, don’t go.  

Ski and Ride with Care and we will see you on the mountain!

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Wednesday, January 7, 2026 6:10 AM – It will be a crisp winter day with temperatures in the low 20s with a breeze and gusts that may impact lift operations. Cloud cover will vary, so expect a mix of sun and clouds. We are expecting 22 lifts to operate today with fun turns off of the summit. Check out Christmas Bowl for pockets that still have some fresh snow. The Panorama Gondola is expected to be on wind hold to start off the day. Enjoy the snow safely by looking out for one another. Please ski with a partner, keep them in sight, and avoid tree wells. Emergency hotline: 760.934.0611

Conditions: Packed powder with powder stashes still to be found.
Visibility: Good visibility with variable cloud cover throughout the day.
Lift status: 22 lifts are expected to operate. Gusts may impact lift operations, The Panorama Gondola is expected to be on wind hold to start off the day.
Safety: Please avoid tree wells and try to land feet first when falling. Always ski and ride in a group and keep them in sight. Learn more about tree wells and Snow Immersion Suffocation. Please give heavy machinery space. Our on-mountain emergency hotline is: 760.934.0611
Road Conditions: The highway is clear, however there are still spots that may be snowy/icy around town, so drive with caution. Check our Road Conditions page for the latest status.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Wednesday January 7, 2026 -- 8:30AM 
Expect all lifts to operate on time under a splattering of clouds today. Winds are expected to pick up throughout the day but shouldn't affect operations. A cold, mostly dry, system will brush by to our north this evening leaving cold temps in its wake tomorrow. High pressure then sets in until at least mid-month.

1/7/26:  7:52 AM Update:
We woke up to a serious overnight dump and the mountain is absolutely stacked. Deep turns, soft landings, and full-on face shots all day long. This is an all-time powder setup! If you’re getting after it, get out early and enjoy the goods while they’re fresh. With that said, heads up out there. Today’s snow is deep and light which means deep snow and tree well immersion risk is high, especially in trees and tighter zones. This is a day to ski with intention. Stick with your buddy, keep each other in sight at all times, and regroup often. If someone goes down, be ready to respond fast and help each other out.

Operations Update: Northway, Gold Hills and Quicksilver will remain closed all day. 

Uphill travel at this time is not permitted. 

Have fun, keep it playful, but ski smart and look out for your crew. 

 Silent flakes stack dreams overnight,
 White forests glowing in morning light.
 Float your turns, let the mountain lead,
 But watch your friends and match their speed.
 Joy runs deep where the snow runs free—
 Ski with care so all return safely.

 Snow depth personally verified, and report written from ground level by Emmy, the avy dog 🐾

Mountain Weather 1/6/2026 4:20pm
Forecaster: Mike Haft

Synopsis: A series of short wave troughs associated with an elongated low, churning in the Gulf of Alaska will continue to pummel the pnw for the next few days. Each wave will bring about 0.50"we every 12hr period delivering much needed snowfall to the mountain. This evening precip intensities will continue to rage along with WSW ridgeline winds. After frontal passage this evening, showers will continue in post frontal showers but will remain intense with hourly snowfall rates exceeding 1"/hr. Wednesday, a secondary front moves through the area although does not look to pack quite the same punch as this evening.

1/7/26: Northway, Gold Hills and Quicksilver will remain closed all day. 

Uphill Travel Status: Uphill travel is NOT permitted. Uphill Status is subject to closure at any time, and travelers must check Uphill Status lights before departure.

⚠️ Snow Immersion Warning ⚠️

Deep, unconsolidated snow conditions today create a high risk of snow immersion suffocation, especially in trees, steep terrain, and terrain traps. A fall into deep snow can make self-rescue extremely difficult and time is critical.

Stay safe out there:
  • Always ski or ride with a partner in sight
  • Stop frequently and regroup
  • Avoid skiing alone in trees or deep features
  • If a partner goes down, respond immediately
  • Carry rescue gear and know how to use it

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
January 7th, 1:55 PM
Good afternoon riders and skiers! It's a powder day! 3-4 inches of dense snow fell overnight, and the snow globe is still shaking and groovin'! The forecast calls for cloudy skies with comfortable temps in the upper 20's at the summit and upper 20's to low 30's at the base by the afternoon.  Come enjoy powder and packed powder conditions earlier in the day, along with variable conditions found on natural terrain as new snow tops frozen surfaces. Snowmaking is on pause today until temps become more conducive.

We will be getting down on 440 skiable acres served by 11 lifts and 106 open trails, with 42 of those getting a fresh corduroy overnight. Check out fan favorite Jester to Spring Fling for a top-tier corduroy experience! Castlerock lift will be spinning today from 9:00 AM - 3:45 PM. North Lynx is scheduled to run starting tomorrow (Thursday) 9:00 AM -3:45 PM as well! All natural terrain is suggested for experts only as base coverage is thin and conditions are variable. Inverness will be closed today for racing events.

Operations have moved back to weekday hours, which means GMX kicks things off, loading at 8:00 AM. Followed by all other scheduled lifts at 9:00 AM. This weekend, look forward to Ikon early ups on Super Bravo loading at 7:30 AM- for Ikon pass holders looking to score some fresh cord and untouched powder before lifts open to the public.  Sugarbush offers a wide range of freestyle parks, whether you’re just starting out or training for competitions, we’ve got you covered. At Mt. Ellen, Riemergasse offers 80 of the finest features on the East Coast, while Lincoln Peak is home to two mini parks featuring 12 creative elements. Sugar Run made its season debut today with 27 features including 3 jumps, bringing out total feature count to 119!

Sharpen Your Swing This Winter! Join PGA Pro Roger King Jan 12th from 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM at the SIM Suites in the SHaRC for exclusive winter golf lessons. Using state-of-the-art simulators, you'll get personalized tips and real-time feedback to improve your swing, accuracy, and overall game. Check out all of our winter events!

All uphill routes are open at both Lincoln Peak and Mt. Ellen, check out our uphill travel policy for more info. *Lincoln Peak evening route will stop at the top of Gate House, due to operations on North Lynx terrain*

Bonjour Tremblant!

 We’re thrilled to announce 100 open trails today, representing 99% of our terrain open! Temperatures are mild, and a light dusting of fresh snow overnight has set the stage for exceptional conditions. With expansive terrain and great weather, today is shaping up to be spectacular!

First Tracks: Access to designated lifts, on North and South side, as early as 7:45 am.

Terrain Park fans will be happy to hear that all 4 parks are open.

Alpine Touring is available today, with access to 15 sections across the mountain.

We can’t wait to welcome you for an unforgettable day on the mountain. See you on the slopes!

Mountain safety tip of the week: Be careful when using the ski lifts.
Knowing how to board ski lifts is essential to ensure the safety of all users.
